1.why: Otherwise/In that case are rare SAT keys; of the two plausible ones, contrast beats Similarly as the harder-to-guess-wrong default.

2.why: Only B states a purpose ('to rule out the possibility that...'), which is exactly what 'explain why they conducted' asks for; the others report results.

3.why: Only D generalizes with the counts a skeptic needs (11 of 12 vents, three oceans) plus the hedged verb 'indicating'.

4.why: Guess among four common transitions; 'Indeed' as the intensifier is the least-used distractor shape here.

5.why: Pure guess; 'Accordingly' (cause-effect) is the most frequent key type in this option family.

6.why: Pure guess; concession 'Even so' sits against three ordinary continuers.

7.why: Only B answers 'why it matters' with reach/impact ('the roughly two-thirds of the world where reliable freezing is unavailable'); A/C/D restate the mechanism or the problem.

8.why: C hedges with a sampled proportion ('9 of the 10 ... indicating'); D self-destructs with 'must be ... every structure the Romans ever built'.

9.why: A is the only hedged aggregate ('modest ... in some settings, though the effects varied'); C and D overclaim, B dismisses.

10.why: Only A spans the whole timeline and names the progression ('Successive innovations steadily lowered'); B/C/D are single isolated steps.

11.why: Only D states significance and forward implication ('oldest DNA ever found ... opens the door'); the others give process or background.

12.why: Guess; 'Consequently' is the commonest key in a set whose other members are contrast/restatement distractors.

13.why: Four options identical except for the number and surface — genuinely at chance.

14.why: Guess; uncommaed options give no clue, so I took the cause-effect member.

15.why: Guess; 'Even so' is the concession against three continuers.

16.why: Guess; 'In fact' as intensifier against contrast/time/result distractors.

17.why: Only A gives stakes/harm ('1.3 million deaths a year ... could again become deadly'); the others give causes or drug-pipeline context.

18.why: Identical sentence frames differing only in count, percent and task — at chance.

19.why: Only D states a finding ('fly nonstop across the Atlantic, up to 2,700 km'); A/B are method, C is background.

20.why: Guess; 'For instance' is the most common key when the set mixes summary, comparison and dismissal.

21.why: Only A gives an ordered series ('first earthquakes, then ground bulging, then a spike in sulfur gas').

22.why: All four are limitations; D names the classic sampling narrowness ('four studios in a single city'), the usual key shape.

23.why: Four parallel limitation frames differing only in percent and scope clause — essentially at chance; took the site-count restriction.

24.why: Guess; 'As a result' is the default key against contrast/similarity/example distractors.
